mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened financial conditions and reduced credit availability.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-move average (t-test p > 0.05), or the Sharpe ratio of SPX 20d returns during the move is not significantly lower than during periods of stable rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate a prolonged easing cycle and lower policy rate cuts.
failure_condition: Over 18 months, the 60-day forward returns during such disinflation episodes are not statistically outperforming a control set of non-disinflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 50,000 jobs triggers a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: During 10 such strong employment months, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 2% in two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to weakening economic momentum and reduced investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the 20-day forward returns during such declines are not statistically lower than during stable production periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (residential construction) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 5% in the same month predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals dual demand expansion in the housing and consumer sectors.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥5% AND RSAFS increases by ≥5% in the same month
failure_condition: During 20 such interaction periods, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months in a labor market recovery regime, the S&P 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive as labor market tightness supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months AND regime_hint='labor market recovery'
failure_condition: Across 10 such recovery episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during baseline recovery periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 (GDP) by at least 2% over a quarter is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate a recessionary environment and capital flight from equities.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: During 8 such contraction quarters, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during stable quarters (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the combination of INDPRO and GDPC1 both fall simultaneously by more than 1% in the same month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to intensified supply-side weakness and investor risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >1% AND GDPC1 decreases by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 12 such interaction events, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during periods of no such dual decline (p > 0.05).
